definition: A neural architecture based on self-attention rather than recurrence or convolution, the foundation of modern LLMs.
details: The Transformer processes entire sequences in parallel, using multi-head self-attention to model pairwise relationships and positional encodings to retain order. Removing recurrence made training dramatically more parallelizable, enabling the scaling that produced GPT, BERT and today’s large language models.
story: You're at a dinner party where everyone is talking at once, and somehow you can still follow the one story being told to you. A Transformer reads a whole sentence in one go, noticing which words matter most to every other word. Instead of moving through words one at a time, like a student reading aloud with a finger under each line, it takes in the whole room and connects the dots. That one trick is what lets computers write, translate and hold conversations the way they do today. The Transformer is the good listener at a loud party — hearing everything at once, and still catching the part that matters.
